# Transcode Video to HLS

- Route: `/tools/transcode-to-hls`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `transcode-to-hls`

## Summary

Package any video into an Apple HLS VOD bundle: master.m3u8, per-rendition .ts segments, ready for the web. (Video tools)

## Details

HTTP Live Streaming serves a video as a playlist of short segments at several quality levels, so a player can start fast and switch rungs as the connection changes. Producing that package by hand means encoding each rendition with aligned keyframes, segmenting them, and writing a master playlist that describes every variant correctly. This page does the whole job: it probes your upload, offers the ladder rungs your source and plan allow, encodes each one with libx264 and AAC into 2 second MPEG-TS segments, optionally adds captions from our own Whisper transcriber, a storyboard sprite sheet and an I-frame playlist for scrubbing, and bundles everything as a tar.gz or zip you can unpack onto any static host.
### What it does
- Probes the source with ffprobe and lists the ladder rungs: 144p, 240p, 360p, 480p, 720p, 1080p and 2160p, each enabled only if the source is tall enough and your plan allows it.
- Encodes each selected rung with libx264 High profile level 4.1 and AAC stereo at 48 kHz, into 2 second .ts segments with a keyframe on every segment boundary.
- Writes hls/master.m3u8 with BANDWIDTH, RESOLUTION, FRAME-RATE and CODECS for every variant, plus one index.m3u8 per rung.
- Optionally transcribes the audio with Whisper into a WebVTT track, translates it into up to 3 more languages with a local model, and links each as a subtitle rendition in the master.
- Optionally renders a storyboard sprite sheet with a WebVTT index for scrubber thumbnails, and always tries to add a 240p I-frame-only playlist.
- Packages the folder with README.txt and report.json into a tar.gz (or zip) and gives you a presigned download link.
### How to use it
1. Upload: The browser uploads straight to our storage bucket with a presigned PUT; the API then downloads it to work on.
2. Probe: ffprobe reads width, height, frame rate, duration and whether there is audio; rungs taller than the source are greyed out.
3. Pick rungs and extras: 360p, 480p and 720p are preselected. Tick captions, extra caption languages, storyboards, and tar.gz or zip.
4. Encode each rung: libx264 at the rung CRF and bitrate with a 2 second GOP, AAC at the rung audio bitrate, HLS VOD output.
5. Add extras and write the master: Captions, storyboards and the I-frame playlist are generated, then master.m3u8 is rewritten to reference them.
6. Download the package: A presigned link valid for 30 minutes by default; the job page lets you fetch it while it lasts.
### Technical details
- The ladder (transcode_profiles.go) is: 144p 200 kbps video and 64 kbps audio, CRF 26; 240p 400/64, CRF 25; 360p 800/96, CRF 23; 480p 1200/128, CRF 23; 720p 2800/128, CRF 22; 1080p 5000/192, CRF 22; 2160p 12000/256, CRF 21. All rungs use the veryfast preset except 2160p, which uses slow.
- Each rung is encoded as ffmpeg -i input -map 0:v:0 -vf scale=-2:H -r FPS -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -level 4.1 -preset P -crf N -sc_threshold 0 -g GOP -keyint_min GOP -b:v B -maxrate 1.2B -bufsize 2B -force_key_frames expr:gte(t,n_forced*2) -map 0:a:0? -c:a aac -b:a A -ac 2 -ar 48000 -hls_time 2 -hls_playlist_type vod -hls_flags independent_segments. GOP is the frame rate times 2, so segments start on keyframes in every rung.
- Because the encode is CRF-driven with -maxrate as a cap, a rung averages at most about its listed bitrate (the cap is 1.2 times it) and comes in lower on easy content. The master playlist advertises BANDWIDTH as the listed video plus audio bitrate, and CODECS as avc1.640028 with mp4a.40.2 appended when audio is present.
- Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block. The server re-validates the rungs at start, so a client cannot request a rung it was not offered.
- Captions use the same Whisper model (whisper-ctranslate2, medium) as the transcriber; the primary track is written to captions/<lang>/auto.vtt with a one-segment subs.m3u8 wrapper and referenced from the master as EXT-X-MEDIA TYPE=SUBTITLES. Up to 3 extra languages from a list of 37 are translated segment by segment by a local Ollama model (a translategemma 12b build); a failed translation is recorded as a warning, never a failed job.
- Storyboards are one ffmpeg pass: fps=1/N with N of 5, 10 or 15 seconds depending on duration (under 10 minutes, under 30, longer), 160 x 90 tiles padded to 16:9 in a 10 x 10 grid per JPEG sprite, plus storyboard.vtt with #xywh cues. The I-frame playlist re-encodes only keyframes at 240p (select=eq(pict_type,I), libx264 CRF 30, 4 second segments) and is listed as EXT-X-I-FRAME-STREAM-INF.
- The master carries EXT-X-VERSION:6, EXT-X-INDEPENDENT-SEGMENTS and three EXT-X-SESSION-DATA entries naming the producer, the site and the copyright holder. report.json records the probe, the variants with segment counts and byte sizes, warnings and timestamps.
### When not to use it
Do not transcode to HLS if you simply want a smaller single file to send or embed; the compressor does that in one pass without segments and playlists. Do not use it for live events, since the output is a finished VOD playlist, not a live origin. Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block. And if your player is a plain video tag with no HLS support, you need an MP4 or an hls.js style player first; a master.m3u8 on its own plays natively only in Safari and on Apple devices.
### Use cases
- Course platforms: Serve lessons from a bucket with adaptive bitrate and captions in several languages.
- Product and marketing pages: Stream a demo without a third-party video host and its player branding.
- Internal portals: Host training videos on your own CDN with scrubber thumbnails.
- Archives: Convert a back catalogue into a streamable layout you control and can mirror.
### FAQ
Q: Which rungs can I select on my plan?
A: Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block. A rung taller than your source is always disabled, because nothing is upscaled. The chips show the reason on hover.
Q: How long are the segments, and why 2 seconds?
A: Every rung is cut into 2 second MPEG-TS segments with a forced keyframe at each boundary, so a player can switch rungs at any segment without a visual glitch. The I-frame playlist uses 4 second segments because it holds only keyframes.
Q: Are the captions linked in the master playlist?
A: Yes. Each language is written as captions/<lang>/auto.vtt with a subs.m3u8 wrapper and declared in master.m3u8 as EXT-X-MEDIA TYPE=SUBTITLES in the subs group, with the source language marked DEFAULT. You can add up to 3 translated languages from the list of 37.
Q: What if my video has no audio?
A: The rungs are encoded video-only with -an, the CODECS attribute omits mp4a.40.2, and the captions step is skipped with a warning in report.json since there is nothing to transcribe.
Q: What is in the package, and how do I host it?
A: hls/master.m3u8, one folder per rung with index.m3u8 and segments, hls/iframes/, optional captions/ and storyboards/, README.txt and report.json. Unpack it onto any static host or bucket that serves .m3u8 and .ts with the right MIME types and point your player at master.m3u8.
Q: How long does the download link work, and can I get tar.gz or zip?
A: The presigned link lasts 30 minutes by default; run the job again if it has expired. Choose tar.gz (the default) or zip in the form before starting.
Q: How long does an HLS transcode take?
A: Each selected rung is a full libx264 encode with the veryfast preset, run one after another, so time grows with duration times the number of rungs; 720p dominates the three default rungs. Captions add a Whisper pass over the whole audio. The job page shows each stage as it completes.
